entries.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: one rehabilitation exercise step photograph, portrait PNG, approximately 1122x1402. Reference image 1 is the previous exercise 114 photograph, used ONLY to match the fixed grey handrail, the woman's white short-sleeve shirt and dark charcoal long trousers, the pale grey-blue studio background and soft photographic lighting. Images 2-4 are the same woman's identity and appearance references. Create a new step 02 photograph for eccentric heel lowering after bilateral calf raise. Camera is fixed at a true SIDE VIEW facing right, CLOSE framing from her waist through BOTH complete knees, calves, ankles and bare feet, plus the supporting hand touching the fixed rail at the upper-right; head deliberately outside the close-up. Both legs nearly straight, both feet shoulder-width apart on a perfectly flat grey-blue floor, offset naturally in depth just enough to see each heel separately. BOTH bare forefeet (balls of feet and relaxed toes) remain firmly planted and BOTH HEELS are lifted together approximately 4 cm at the TOP of a comfortable bilateral calf raise. It is crucial to show TWO lifted heels and TWO grounded forefeet; neither foot is lifted entirely. No external weight, no step or platform. One hand lightly rests on the same fixed matte gray waist-height handrail to the right; natural arm segment and hand visible at top. Human anatomy and leg lengths natural, dark trousers reach above bare ankles. Preserve the backdrop/soft light from references. Single pose, continuous photographic image. No text, numbers, arrows, diagram, borders, montage or inset. Foot and heel gaps should be large enough for teaching. Keep toes and heels fully inside frame.

entries.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: exercise 114 step 03, one rehabilitation studio photograph. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the accepted step 02 bilateral heel-rise photograph. Make ONLY the necessary change from two feet supporting at the top to ONE training foot supporting at the top: keep the NEAR-camera leg nearly straight and its forefoot/toes in EXACTLY the same ground contact place; keep its heel raised at EXACTLY the same comfortable height. The far-camera non-training leg now bends gently at the knee, moves its lower leg backwards toward the left of the image, and lifts the ENTIRE far foot completely clear of the flat floor. Show an obvious air gap of about 8 cm beneath that far foot, located behind and to the LEFT of the near training calf, without overlap with the near bare foot. The far foot stays relaxed and natural, NOT bearing any weight, with five normal toes. This is transfer at the TOP after rising on both feet; the near training heel MUST remain clearly elevated and must not lower yet. Preserve everything else exactly: same side close view from waist through both complete knees/legs/feet, same hand resting on grey fixed handrail, white T-shirt hem, charcoal long pants, natural knee/ankle continuity, floor shadows and pale grey-blue photographic background, same camera/focal length/framing and person size. No weight, no step, no platform, no jumping. Only one static pose, no arrows, labels, text, inset or collage. Output portrait PNG same 1122x1402 frame as target.

REMOVE ONLY the erroneous extra grounded FAR foot and its narrow lower trouser leg that are visible immediately BEHIND/right of the main supporting bare foot. There must be EXACTLY TWO legs and TWO bare feet after editing: (1) the MAIN NEAR leg centered, nearly straight, with forefoot planted and heel raised, retained unchanged; (2) the OTHER leg bent backwards to the LEFT with its one foot already suspended in air, retained unchanged. The woman has ONE standing support foot only. Preserve the existing bent airborne limb to the left, preserve both real knees, main training heel raise height, natural leg continuity, trousers, same hand on grey fixed rail, white shirt, side-close framing, grey-blue background, soft light and camera. KEEP the OTHER foot clearly airborne behind to the LEFT; it MUST NOT return to floor at this step. Maintain exactly two real legs, no duplicated leg behind the support shin, no third foot. Preserve side-close framing from waist through both complete knees and feet, same natural limb lengths and proportions, same white shirt/charcoal trousers, hand on grey fixed support rail, background/floor color, shadows/soft light and camera scale. The rail stays perfectly fixed in same location; hand can naturally slide a tiny amount down it with lowering. No weight, no step. The final sole is fully FLAT, not hovering, not remaining on tiptoe. Same 1122x1402 portrait PNG, no labels, arrows, text or collage.

Edit image 1 into a FOOT-AND-KNEE CLOSE VIEW of the starting posture. A single stable seated posture on the SAME sturdy matte gray armless chair, pelvis seated on the chair seat, torso upright, hands relaxed palm-down on each thigh. No external weight, no pads on knees, no equipment. Both knees comfortably bent at approximately a right angle; both lower legs upright. BOTH BARE FEET completely flat on the floor: each heel, full forefoot and relaxed toes clearly on the floor, ankles neutral, feet parallel and comfortably separated.
Camera: side view from the same woman's left side with only a slight front offset so BOTH knees and BOTH entire feet can be distinctly seen, facing image right. Frame from lower chest through thighs, both knees and complete lower legs down to the full bare toes and heels; include the stable chair seat and its legs/contact with floor. The feet and knees are larger than in the original full-body view. Face/head may be out of frame for this local exercise detail. Allow modest floor margin below both feet and right-side explanatory space. Approximately 1122 x 1402 portrait aspect ratio. Natural adult proportions; fingers/toes anatomically correct. White shirt/dark charcoal trousers, photographic texture and soft gray-blue studio seamless floor, lighting and chair material remain consistent with image 1 and references.
Critical visible step: BOTH full foot soles are resting on floor, neither heel lifted; thigh/knee position stable, hands naturally resting, toes do not grip. One woman, one pose, one chair, no inset, no multiple panels, no text, no labels, no arrows, no watermarks.

Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: a single photorealistic rehabilitation exercise step photo for T-LOW-038, step 116-s01, the START of resisted RIGHT ankle dorsiflexion.
Input images: reference-01.png, reference-02.png, reference-03.png are visual identity / clothes / lighting references ONLY. Use the same adult East Asian woman, natural warm skin, black ponytail, white short-sleeved T-shirt, charcoal dark grey trousers. Change her exercise pose as specified.
Scene: clean muted blue-grey seamless studio and blue-grey floor, soft even studio light, real shadows, a low light-grey exercise mat.
Pose and exercise: she is in LONG SITTING on the mat, both legs extended straight forward with natural soft unlocked knees. The RIGHT leg is closest to the camera and is the exercising leg; the LEFT leg is farther from the camera, resting unbanded. A small low light-grey soft cushion supports ONLY the right calf. The RIGHT heel and ankle project beyond the distal end of this cushion, letting the ankle move freely. The right shin and knee remain supported and stationary. Bare feet. The right ankle is at an ordinary neutral starting position: the right forefoot is roughly perpendicular (90 degrees) to the shin, not actively pulled back, not strongly pointed down; all five toes are relaxed, natural and visible.
Resistance setup: one wide flat blue-green elastic exercise band wraps securely around the BALL OF THE RIGHT FOOT at the metatarsal / forefoot region, below the toes, never strangling or covering the toes. Its two flat strands travel FORWARD AWAY FROM HER BODY, beyond the toe end in the same direction as the shin's long axis, and join a small low stable heavy GREY FLOOR ANCHOR BASE immediately in front of the right foot. Show the entire low anchor base and the visible fastening point clearly; the base rests firmly on the floor outside the mat. The anchor must be directly beyond the right foot in the direction the feet point, not to either side and not under her leg. The band has mild visible tension without forcefully deforming skin. Her hands do NOT hold the band. Nothing is connected to her face, neck, torso, left leg, or foot cushion.
Camera: fixed right-front slightly elevated oblique SIDE close view. The photo is portrait, about 1122 x 1402 pixels, framing the complete right knee, whole right shin, cushion, heel, ankle, complete toes, band's full path, and anchor. Include enough partial thighs / mat and the far left leg to prove long sitting. Prioritize a clear right-foot side profile showing the foot-shin angle and its movement plane; knee and foot must not be cropped. Right shin runs diagonally from upper left to lower right; foreground right ankle and forefoot are central-lower, front anchor farther beyond them toward the right-bottom of frame. No need to show her whole head for this local ankle task, but any visible body must match the references.
Natural body proportions, correct connected knee-calf-ankle-foot anatomy, exactly two feet, five toes each, uninjured real skin and fabric. This is one clear neutral-start pose, a photograph, not a collage. NO text, NO numbers, NO arrows, NO diagram overlay, NO logos, NO watermark. Do not show a chair or standing position.

independent_reviews.findings: 握带来自身体方向；右踝中立→前下推；右跟越过垫边和软垫支持可见；动作/带位/比例可用。
右侧测试足近镜，外侧锚点在近镜前景、与远侧左足相反侧；带位/中立足/软垫/足比例清楚。

limitations: 画面验收仅确认可见体位、方向、支撑、器械和比例；不证明实际带张力、韧带应力、肌力等级、疗效或临床许可。
局部近景不完整展示脸部/马尾，身份由三个参考输入锁定及可见肤色、体形、服装一致性支持，未将不可见面部细节标为已直接核验。
照片表达姿态差异，不给出真实测量的踝角度；prompt中的角度仅是制作姿态控制提示。
生成锚座是视觉示范道具；实际固定可靠性不能由静态照片验证。
画面审查仅针对可见姿势、人体比例与器材/支撑接触；不证明实际负荷、肌肉发力、临床适用性、下降速度、保持时长或测量精度。
局部近景按清单保留相关膝、小腿、踝足和必要躯干/手位；面部多在画外，身份由三参考与原图锁定。116-s01/s02远侧非活动左足外缘有局部裁切，测试右足完整。
116按方向分别设置，不能将本轮五帧当作连续动作。
preservation: 没有覆盖旧单图/旧步骤图或共享进度JSON；未修改正式应用、版本、桌面快捷方式或Git。
